name: CWV
description: Self-hosted real-user Core Web Vitals tracking (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB) that correlates each measurement with Drupal-side signal (route, role, cache state, query count, render-tree size) via an extensible tagged-service collector contract.

suggests.drupal/lscache: Adds an LSCache hit/miss + tag-list collector for the cwv_lscache submodule.
suggests.drupal/jelastic_info: Adds a Jelastic environment-state collector for the cwv_jelastic submodule.

project_description: CWV is a self-hosted Real User Monitoring tool for Core Web Vitals. The bundled beacon JS captures LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, and TTFB from real visitor browsers and POSTs them to an in-Drupal endpoint (/cwv/beacon); nothing is sent to any third-party service. Measurements land in the cwv_beacons table, and cron-driven synthetic observations land in cwv_probes. A report at /admin/reports/cwv renders correlation panels that join each metric to backend signals: page/dynamic cache HIT vs MISS, backend cache miss count, render-tree (cache-tag) size, database query count, plus per-route p50/p75/p95 percentiles and daily counts with operator-recorded deploy-event markers. Capture is off after install; sampling defaults to 0.1; per-IP flood protection, a max_rows table-size guard, and outlier filtering defend the endpoint; three URL-storage policies (hash / path / full) bound PII exposure. The module is built as a substrate: a tagged-service collector contract with four shapes (synchronous, async-decoration, probe, panel-contribution) lets sibling modules add their own context fields and report panels. Built-in collectors cover Drupal cache state, user auth state, backend cache hit/miss, render-tree size, database query counts, OPcache and APCu runtime health, edge-cache state across major CDN vendors, and upstream/CDN request-ID correlation.
